newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain snubs Cuba at Ibero-American meeting.
newsitem.headline: Spain snubs Cuba at Ibero-American meeting.

text.p: A senior Spanish official, in a new snub to Cuba, said on Thursday that only countries which seek liberty will be welcome at future meetings of Ibero-American parliamentarians.

Communist-ruled Cuba stayed away from the Conference of Presidents of Democratic Ibero-American Parliaments meeting in Madrid which began on Wednesday, angered by a Spanish invitation to attend only as an observer.

"We will not hesitate to cordially and passionately invite to coming conferences each and all of the Ibero-American peoples who are truly and sincerely seeking liberty," Spanish parliament president Federico Trillo told the visiting parliamentarians.
The conference was the latest source of tension between Spain and its former colony Cuba.

Relations have soured since the centre-right government of Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar took power one year ago, insisting much more adamantly than its Socialist predecessor on democratic reforms in Cuba.

The president of Cuba's parliament, Ricardo Alarcon, responded to the conference invitation earlier this month by saying Spain was acting as if it were still the island's colonial master by trying to downgrade its status.
But many of the 19 presidents of parliaments attending the conference supported Spain's position.

"With most respect, in a conference of presidents of democratic parliaments it would not make sense for Cuba to participate because it is not a democracy," said Ramon Guillermo Aveledo, president of Venezuela's Chamber of Deputies.
"Here today, there is dissension, but there is not in the Cuban parliament."
Mexican delegate Genovevo Figueroa Zamudio defended Cuba's right to attend, saying it was important for all Ibero-American countries to be present at coming conferences.
